Paste these prompts into Claude or ChatGPT, in order, or open a ready report on your ticker.

1Set up the chat

Three prompts, pasted once at the start of a chat. Switch web search on first (in ChatGPT: Search).

1 · The rules. Paste it first in every chat, or save it in a Project’s instructions.

2 · The documents. In our test, the web tool read only 100,000 of about 370,000 characters of each CrowdStrike annual report, so this prompt asks Claude to say how much it read.

3 · The answer format. If you don’t ask for a form, Claude picks one: often long, full of adjectives, with numbers that have no period or unit.

Which Claude? Sonnet is enough; Opus for long multi-report chats.

Swaps the prompts in stages 3 and 4.

2The business

What does the company sell, to whom, and what keeps rivals out?

Claude finds this in: the 10-K (the annual report) and the earnings releases.

3The numbers

Is the business growing, and how much cash does it really keep?

Version for: Other (most companies) · change

Claude finds this in: the 10-K, the 10-Q (the quarterly report) and the earnings releases.

Bank (JPMorgan)

The trap for this type: Free cash flow means nothing for a bank

Insurer (Chubb)

The trap for this type: Premium growth can hide a bad claims year; released reserves can flatter one

Property trust (Realty Income)

The trap for this type: Net income and P/E (see the example in stage 4)

Oil & gas (ExxonMobil)

The trap for this type: Last year's profit is last year's oil price: its realised liquids price fell to $55.30 a barrel in 2025

Miner (Barrick)

The trap for this type: Revenue follows the metal price: gold rose 44 % in 2025 while Barrick produced about 3.26 million ounces and its AISC came in above guidance

Biotech / no revenue yet

The trap for this type: P/E: there are no earnings

Software (CrowdStrike)

The trap for this type: The adjusted profit (see the example in stage 3)

A report shows free cash flow both ways, as the company defines it and after stock pay, each with its source: open one free

4What you pay

Is the price fair for what the business earns?

Version for: Other (most companies) · change

Claude finds this in: the earnings releases and the 10-K for the numbers; the price is the one you give.

Bank (JPMorgan)

Property trust (Realty Income)

The exact price at the moment of the sum comes from a licensed feed: give Claude the price and its date. Every report uses one open one free

5Who runs it

Who runs the company, who owns it, and are insiders selling?

Claude finds this in: the proxy statement, the Form 4 filings (insider trades) and the 10-K.

6The risks

What could go wrong, and what outside forces move the results?

Claude finds this in: the 10-K (risk factors, legal proceedings, notes) of the last two years.

  • London: prices are in pence (1,000p ÷ 50p = 20×, not 2,000×)
  • TSMC: 1 US share = 5 Taiwan shares
  • NVIDIA: fiscal 2026 ended in January 2026

Part (5) handles this.

7The market and the analysts

What has the price done, and what do the analysts think?

Claude finds this in: the price history of any free quote site (you paste it) and the exchange's short-interest list.

Analyst ratings and price targets are sold under licence (FactSet, LSEG, S&P Capital IQ): no prompt reaches them. Every report includes them open one free

8Check every answer

Check 2 catches the most frequent error: a real number that answers a different question. A quarter cannot pass as a year once Claude has to name the period.

Real number, wrong thing the most frequent

  • CrowdStrike free cash flow, asked plainly: Claude gave the latest quarter, $377.4 million. The year was $1,235.3 million.
  • CrowdStrike, fiscal 2026: a profit of $1.05 billion on its own The company's own version of profit, which leaves out costs such as stock pay. measure, but a loss of $293.3 million under Profit that follows the official accounting rules..

Invented number

Microsoft’s Bing AI demo (Feb 2023) gave Gap’s operating margin as 5.9 %. The real figure was 4.6 %.

Hidden orders in a page

In the Guardian’s test of ChatGPT search (Dec 2024), text hidden on a page ordered a favourable review: it wrote entirely positive summaries. The rules prompt tells Claude to ignore such orders.

9What a report adds

Four things no prompt gets you:

  • Analyst ratings and price targets Licensed data, so no prompt can fetch it.
  • Up to 8 call transcripts What management said, not only the numbers.
  • The exact price and a dated exchange rate Nothing guessed from memory.
  • Every number with its source Checked before the report is published.

10FAQ

Is Claude free for stock research?

Yes, with limits. The Free plan gives Sonnet, with usage limits every 5 hours and every week. Opus needs Pro ($17 a month billed yearly, or $20 monthly).

Can Claude read a 10-K?

Yes. Upload it, or turn on web search and give it the EDGAR link. Ask about one Item at a time and make it quote the sentence. A chat takes up to 20 uploaded files.

Can Claude give me analyst estimates or a live price?

No. Analyst consensus is sold by FactSet, LSEG and S&P Capital IQ, and a price from a web page may be days old. Give Claude the price yourself, with its date.

Is a MyStockButler report investment advice?

No. It is research: the company’s numbers, each with its source, and what they mean. It never tells you to buy or sell.

NVIDIA (NVDA)

MyStockButler Research TeamUpdated Oct 16, 2026
Important investment disclaimer

This article is general information, not investment advice. It is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold any security and it does not take your personal circumstances into account. MyStockButler and the authors hold no position in NVDA. Analysis date: October 16, 2026. Figures can be outdated after that date; verify material facts and consult a qualified adviser before investing.

Executive Summary

What the business is

NVIDIA sells connected computing platforms—GPUs, networking, systems and software—to cloud providers, server makers and businesses. A GPU is a processor that handles many tasks at once; a cloud provider rents computing power and storage over the internet. Fiscal 2026 revenue was $215,938 million, led by Data Center. A dollar comes in when a direct customer buys a platform or software, while a cloud provider may rent its resulting capacity to an AI company or business. Software may be licensed, subscribed to or included with hardware.

  • Concentration: Data Center produced $193,737 million in fiscal 2026, versus $16,042 million from Gaming and $2,349 million from Automotive.
  • Platform economics: A sale can bundle GPUs, networking and CUDA, NVIDIA’s software tools for programming GPUs. NVIDIA does not disclose separate software revenue or renewal rates.
  • Outsourced production: NVIDIA designs products but relies on specialists for fabrication, packaging, memory, testing and assembly. Supply and capacity commitments reached $279 billion at July 2026.
  • Cash timing: Sales can precede cash. Days sales outstanding reached 60 days, and five direct customers represented 70% of accounts receivable at July 2026.

The challenges

  • Customer payback: Cloud providers must recover equipment, networking, power, cooling, staff and financing costs through paid workloads or savings. Low utilization or weak returns could pause the next spending cycle.
  • Platform substitution: CUDA familiarity can make switching costly, but customers may port workloads to AMD ROCm or custom chips. The risk is greatest if alternatives deliver better economics on real workloads.
  • System delivery and supply: A platform needs processors, memory, networking, assembly, power and cooling to arrive together. NVIDIA’s $279 billion of commitments increases the cost of a demand or product mismatch.
  • Export restrictions: Policy can block sales after inventory and supplier commitments are in place. NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion H20 charge after U.S. export restrictions.
